profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting for a draft conference submission on DesiGNN, a framework that uses structured knowledge priors plus LLM-based literature elicitation to generate strong initial GNN designs for unseen datasets. The meeting takes place two weeks before camera-ready submission after the internal benchmark suite and paper draft have been assembled. The agenda is to review whether the current experimental and methodological presentation is 'ready' for external coauthor circulation: specifically the evidence for the claimed top-5.77% initial proposals, the description of the knowledge bank construction pipeline, and what materials need to be packaged for reproducibility. The expected outcome is a go/no-go decision on approving the current design and a short list of modifications before sending the draft to collaborators.

members.name: Dr. Linh Tran
members.expertise: AutoML for graph learning, benchmark methodology, research framing
members.background: Leads a university ML research group focused on automated model design for non-Euclidean data and has published several benchmark-heavy papers on graph representation learning.
members.private_state: Wants the design review to conclude that the paper is mature enough to circulate to external coauthors this week, while minimizing requests for additional experiments that could delay submission.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says the method is 'ready', that means the scientific story, key ablations, and headline results are stable enough for paper circulation even if engineering artifacts are still rough.
The 'benchmark suite' refers to the internal 42-dataset collection after the group's standard filtering rules removed pathological or low-signal datasets.

A result described as an 'initial proposal' is the first model produced after allowing the system to instantiate its default knowledge retrieval and template-filling pipeline, without any human tuning but including its built-in warm-start logic.

For reproducibility in a design-review context, it is sufficient to provide the deterministic experiment config bundle and pseudo-code for the knowledge construction process; packaging the full retrieval index can come later.
A sensitivity check on noisy descriptions can be shown with representative perturbation families rather than exhaustive regeneration across every benchmark dataset.

members.name: Sara Kim
members.expertise: Evaluation pipelines, reproducibility infrastructure, LLM-augmented retrieval systems
members.background: Builds the lab's experiment orchestration and artifact release workflows, and previously worked on industry-facing model evaluation where replication standards were strict.
members.private_state: Wants to prevent the paper from being reviewed as underspecified or irreproducible, and is quietly looking for places where the current draft overstates how turnkey the system is.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says the method is 'ready', that means an external collaborator could rerun the core pipeline from the released artifacts without lab-internal setup knowledge.
The 'benchmark suite' means the full curated corpus that appears in the spreadsheet, including the few datasets excluded from aggregate tables but still used in stress checks.

An 'initial proposal' should mean the very first architecture emitted before any retrieval-conditioned refinement or fallback heuristics are applied, because those are already part of downstream search assistance.
Reproducibility for this paper requires releasing the concrete retrieval index, prompt templates, and benchmark-specific preprocessing manifests, not just high-level configs.
If the paper claims robustness to noisy descriptions, the review-standard expectation is that the perturbation protocol is applied uniformly to every dataset reported in the main aggregate claim.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the draft/design is 'ready' or 'not ready' for external coauthor review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the scientific narrative and main empirical support are sufficiently stable for collaborators to comment on positioning and minor gaps.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the pipeline and artifacts are specified well enough that an external collaborator could actually reproduce the core claims without unwritten lab conventions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML research design reviews, 'ready' is a routine shorthand and both participants are cooperative; each hears the other as discussing the same publication-readiness threshold, not different standards.

misalignment_points.topic: Which benchmark collection 'the benchmark suite' refers to
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to results holding 'across the benchmark suite' or 'on the full suite'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the 42-dataset internal benchmark set after the lab's standard exclusions for degenerate labels, missing metadata, and unstable splits.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the broader spreadsheet-backed corpus, including the handful of stress-test datasets that were omitted from headline aggregates but still exist in the evaluation repository.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both collections are commonly called 'the suite' within the lab, and the excluded datasets are peripheral enough that neither expects the other to be referencing a different subset.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss the claim that DesiGNN gives a strong 'initial proposal' for unseen datasets.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the first architecture output after the system performs its standard retrieval-and-prior assembly steps and applies built-in warm-start defaults.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the raw first architecture suggestion before retrieval-conditioned refinement, fallback expansion, or default heuristic adjustments are applied.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds self-explanatory and both regard the retrieval stage as part of the normal system, but one counts it as pre-proposal setup while the other counts it as post-proposal assistance.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to include a 'reproducibility package' before circulation/submission.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this package covers configs, seeds, pseudo-code, and enough process description for reviewers to understand the method, with release-hardening deferred.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this package includes runnable manifests, the retrieval index snapshot, prompt variants, and preprocessing artifacts needed to recreate the reported numbers exactly.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Reproducibility packaging is usually treated as a support item rather than a headline design decision, so both use the same phrase while silently importing different boundaries for what is included.

I need to keep us focused on the highest-leverage fixes so we don't accidentally open the door to a new experimental cycle.
